summary.intent: Act on recommendations for three pending items in the caliper project: decide how to handle body-less components (change 8), clone real-library corpora (Chakra, react-spectrum), and validate PRs #505 and #506 with real-corpus measurements before merge. The user then asked to proceed autonomously and token-efficiently.
summary.outcome: Cloned Chakra and react-spectrum into a shared cache, measured #506 against main on real Chakra (629 components, no row changes, 1.24 vs 1.30 GiB, 5.4 vs 5.1 s) and added the result to the PR body. Sized change 7 on react-spectrum, verified hook hand-off behavior, and committed a 'Known limits (alpha)' README bullet on a new branch.

repo: Corpora are set up via corpora.py setup with --corpora pointing to a shared cache (~/.cache/caliper/corpora), so worktrees don't re-clone; the cache is re-creatable and safe to delete.

Product rule: ambient attributes like className/style stay as names unless the component body uses them. Body-less .d.ts components therefore don't show className/style in Controls, which affects most real design-system libraries.
Resolver/checker-walk changes require checking peak memory and time on Chakra (project rule), not only fixture numbers.
packages/storybook/README.md has a 'Known limits (alpha)' section, the established place for plain statements of what's missing.
Chakra corpus is about 4.2 GB when cloned and installed with pnpm, at a pinned commit.
CI on #505 and #506 was green except Entire Gates, which waits on approval.

code.finding: Added a bullet under 'Known limits (alpha)' documenting that when a component body hands props to a hook (useX(props)), className/style are not detected as used. Verified with a temporary fixture before writing.

workflow: Interleave baseline and candidate runs, and check main is deterministic against itself, before attributing output diffs to a PR.
Build the baseline by archiving origin/main into a separate directory and building it in the background while other work (clones) proceeds, then measure only when the machine is quiet.
Verify actual behavior with a temporary fixture (then delete it) before documenting a limitation.
Run the lint gate on docs changes before committing.

friction: The measurement had to wait for the clone and baseline build to finish so the machine was quiet enough for meaningful timing/memory numbers.
Entire Gates CI check blocks on approval, so it can't be cleared autonomously.
The temporary fixture was written inside a worktree (fixtures/_tmp_hook) and had to be cleaned up afterward.
open_items: Add a note in output that the component body wasn't analysed for .d.ts (body-less) components, so the className/style gap is stated rather than silent (change 8 follow-up).
User still needs to review and merge #505 (docs only) and #506 (now with real Chakra numbers).
Change 7 sizing on react-spectrum: scan7.py was run, but results are not reported in the transcript and the decision isn't recorded.
The docs-bullet commit is on a new branch off main; push/PR not yet done.
The other three corpora and the oracle run are deferred until after the merged batch.
Whether to add className to Controls for all components remains a separate rule-change decision.
